summary: Iter36y — Auto-relance cron + per-client toggle + manual trigger + history: full E2E verified. Backend 37/37 pytest pass (6 new tests in test_iter36y_auto_relance.py + 31 regression Iter36u/v/w/x). Master toggle/day-of-week/grace_days/email persist via PUT /api/admin/settings. POST /api/cashier/overdue/relance-auto-run is admin-only (regular user => 403), bypasses master toggle for manual triggers, persists each run in db.auto_relance_runs, and targets ONLY business_clients with auto_relance_enabled=True (opt-out clients correctly excluded). GET /api/cashier/overdue/relance-history returns history. BusinessClient POST defaults auto_relance_enabled=False; setting True is persisted. Frontend smoke: /portal/cash renders 6 tabs for admin (Caisse, Facturation, Catalogue, Clients en compte, Modes de paiement, Relance auto). Relance auto tab shows master toggle + Lundi select + grace_days (30) + email field + Enregistrer + 'Tester maintenant' + history table (9 entries after trigger). Clients en compte form shows the '🔔 Relance automatique des impayés' full-width checkbox. No backend or frontend issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: CashBilling.jsx is now 1064 lines — consider splitting per tab (ReceiptsTab/InvoicesTab/CatalogTab/BusinessTab/PaymentTab/AutoRelanceTab) into individual files under /pages/portal/cash/ to keep each module <500 lines. Not blocking but recommended for maintainability.
AutoRelanceTab fetches GET /api/admin/settings on mount — fine, but if PUT response returns the updated settings, prefer using that response directly rather than re-fetching to reduce a round-trip.

test_cron_skips_when_master_disabled writes directly to db.settings via pymongo; assertion is loose ('skipped in (None, False) or reason != master_disabled'). It's defensible since manual bypass is the contract, but a follow-up test calling _run_auto_relance_cashier in-process with a fixed weekday would harden the cron path coverage.
Backend run history is stored unbounded in db.auto_relance_runs — consider TTL index or a retention policy (e.g., 180 days) to prevent collection growth.
